subject: Re: Prepaid overlay + overspill repricing — QuickCart
messages:
From: Ivy Zhou <ivy.zhou@quickcart.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quickcart.com
Date: 2026-12-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Short-term capacity cover for Dec 29-31 spike

Hi Vanessa / Laura,

QuickCart has an expected traffic surge for Dec 29-31 (marketing promotion + mobile app push). We should be within our committed baseline for the month, but the spike will likely push us ~45% above our daily quota for a ~72 hour window.

We need a temporary, pre-approved capacity overlay that: 1) gives us a guaranteed throughput uplift for the 72h window, 2) includes straightforward invoicing (pro-forma ok), and 3) limits the overrun rate so our ops team can plan.

Questions: can Redwood offer a prepaid slab that sits on top of our commit (billed up-front or as a PO), and a capped overspill surcharge if we exceed that slab? Also, any short-term discount if we commit to a small multi-week ramp afterwards?

Attaching a simple volume estimate: QuickCart_proforma.xlsx (see attachment stub). Procurement looped on cc.

Thanks,
Ivy
Ivy Zhou
Head of Platform Ops, QuickCart
ivy.zhou@quickcart.com

Attachments: QuickCart_proforma.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Zhou <ivy.zhou@quickcart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity cover for Dec 29-31 spike

Hi Ivy — thanks for the heads-up and the workbook. We can definitely put a short-term construct together. High-level proposal that we can turn into a pro-forma quickly: 

- Prepaid slab overlay: purchase a fixed slab sized for the 72h spike (examples: 100k tokens / 500k tokens) billed as a one-time prepay or PO.
- Overspill repricing: if usage exceeds the slab during the window, overspill billed at a capped overrun rate (we propose a 20% premium over your current per-token rate).
- Deferred true-up: we can bill the prepay immediately (or accept a PO with payment terms), then do a single true-up invoice at the end of the month if actual overrun differs from the slab.
- Introductory uplift discount: if QuickCart commits to a 3-week staged capacity increase post-spike, we can offer a 15% discount on overspill charges for the first billing cycle.

I’ll pull finance/legal in for the PO and amendment language (Ben for finance, Laura to coordinate account ops). If that sounds directionally right I’ll generate a pro-forma and a short amendment for signature.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0196

Attachments: redwood_amendment_draft.docx (draft, 18KB stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Short-term capacity cover for Dec 29-31 spike

Vanessa / Laura — putting finance notes here so procurement has clarity.

- Prepay vs PO: we can accept a PO with Net30 for the slab. If customer prefers immediate payment we can invoice.
- Accounting treatment: label as "prepaid capacity credit"; any unused slab volume at month-end rolls forward to a 30-day buffer (not to exceed 25% of the slab) — after that it expires.
- Discount treatment: a 15% discount on overspill for the first post-spike invoice is fine. If QuickCart wants a deeper discount (>=25%) we need a short-term commitment (3 months min).

For legal: will need a one-page amendment (service addendum) referencing the existing MSA with the slab size, dates, overspill cap, and invoicing path. Laura, can you coordinate the version for signature?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
